item.title: Molecular pendulum shuttles protons to enable rapid hydrogen production in enzymes
item.description: Nearly all metabolic processes require protons—positively charged hydrogen atoms. Although these are abundant in the cellular fluid, the biocatalysts involved depend on mechanisms for efficiently capturing protons and transporting them to the site where catalysis occurs. Enzymes from microorganisms can produce hydrogen (H₂) by combining electrons with protons. These so-called hydrogenases are so efficient that one biocatalyst can capture nearly 10,000 protons per second. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New 'hunter-killer' chemistry captures and destroys forever chemicals
item.description: They can turn up in a nonstick frying pan, a waterproof jacket, a takeout food wrapper or the foam used to fight fires. Known as "forever chemicals," these substances are ubiquitous in modern society, prized for their extreme durability and versatility. However, their charm comes with a curse: They are so durable they resist degradation, posing threats to human health and the environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: ‘Crucial opportunity to act’ as study finds most of Europe’s wild bee species in decline
item.description: As Cop17 kicks off, records since 1921 show more bee species declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alps Most of Europe’s wild bee species and about half of its hover fly species have declined over the last century, a study has found, as a UN biodiversity summit begins in Armenia. Records since 1921 show more bee species are declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alpine region. The richness of bee and hover fly species suffered a persistent drop in the Atlantic and Continental regions, the study found, though trends in other regions were mixed or even… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. item.title: Smart farming is already proving profitable in some regions, global analysis finds
item.description: The use of robots, drones and AI tools in agriculture is already paying off on 42% of the world's cropland. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Auroral structure could be caused by bouncing electrons
item.description: The aurora is among nature's most visually striking phenomena. It occurs when charged particles from the sun are funneled by Earth's magnetic field into the upper atmosphere, where they collide with atoms and molecules and produce distinctly colored curtainlike patterns of light. Fuente: Phys.org.
